title: Chapter 28. Nagari Padas — II: Vasu Ghosha (padas from GPT), Nayanananda, Yadu, Murari, Balarama Dasa, Chandrashekhara, Lochana Dasa
html:
On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27.

1. Vasu Ghosha — "ki herinu ogo sai bidagadha-rāja…" (KGC 5.1; GPT1 p. 162, no. 16)

Nagari-bhava (only in the address to a friend). "What have I seen, friend — the king of those versed in rasa!" Gaura is the wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees in the midst of Navadvipa: its branches are love, its leaves anuraga, its flowers longing, its fruit pure prema, from which rasa flows without end; the devotees, like birds and bees, taste it, the tree's shade nourishes all — only the poet is deprived through his own fault. In KGC it is the gaura-chandrika to the 5th kshanada. Raga suhai-deshag.1

কি হেরিনু ওগো সই বিদগধ-রাজ ।
ভকত-কলপতরু নবদ্বীপ মাঝ ॥

ki herinu ogo sai bidagadha-rāja |
bhakata-kalapataru nabadvīpa mājha ||

ki herinu — what have I seen; ogo sai — O friend; bidagadha-rāja — the king of the vidagdhas (those versed in rasa); bhakata-kalapataru — the wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees; nabadvīpa mājha — in the midst of Navadvipa

1.1What have I seen, friend! — the king of those versed in rasa,
the wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees in the midst of Navadvipa.2

পিরীতির শাখা সব অনুরাগ-পাতে ।
কুসুম আরতি তাহে জগত মোহিতে ॥

pirītira śākhā saba anurāga-pāte |
kusuma ārati tāhe jagata mohite ||

pirītira śākhā saba — all its branches are love; anurāga-pāte — with leaves of anuraga; kusuma ārati — its flowers are longing (ārati); tāhe — on it; jagata mohite — to enchant the world

1.2Its branches are love, its leaves are anuraga,
its flowers are longing, to enchant the world.

নিরমল প্রেম-ফল ফলে সর্বকাল ।
এক ফলে নব রস ঝরয়ে অপার ॥

niramala prema-phala phale sarvakāla |
eka phale naba rasa jharaye apāra ||

niramala prema-phala — the pure fruit of prema; phale sarvakāla — ripens at all times; eka phale — from a single fruit; naba rasa — fresh (or: ninefold) rasa; jharaye apāra — flows without end

1.3At all times the pure fruit of prema ripens on it;
from a single fruit ever-fresh rasa flows without end.3

ভকত চাতক পিক শুক অলি হংস ।
নিরবধি বিলসয়ে রস পরশংস ॥

bhakata cātaka pika śuka ali haṃsa |
nirabadhi bilasaye rasa paraśaṃsa ||

bhakata — the devotees; cātaka pika śuka ali haṃsa — chatakas, cuckoos, parrots, bees, swans; nirabadhi — ceaselessly; bilasaye — delight; rasa paraśaṃsa — praising the rasa

1.4The devotees — chatakas, cuckoos, parrots, bees, swans —
ceaselessly delight in it, praising its rasa.

স্থির চর সুর নর যার ছায়া পোষে ।
বাসুদেব বঞ্চিত আপন কর্ম-দোষে ॥

sthira cara sura nara yāra chāyā poṣe |
bāsudeba bañcita āpana karma-doṣe ||

sthira cara — the unmoving and the moving; sura nara — gods and men; yāra chāyā poṣe — whose shade nourishes; bāsudeba bañcita — Vasudeva is deprived; āpana karma-doṣe — through the fault of his own deeds

1.5The unmoving and the moving, gods and men, are nourished by its shade —
only Vasudeva is deprived through the fault of his own deeds.4

"śrīgauracandrasya" (gaura-chandrika), raga suhai-deshag, p. 34 (scan PDF p. 66). GPT1 — p. 162, no. 16 (raga suhai or desharaga; scan PDF p. 421); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 16 (catalogue: VG-020). The pada is not in PK. The catalogue listed it as "GPT only"; the KGC witness was found in preparing this chapter (attribution to Vasu by KGC and GPT, A). In GPT the pada stands in the section of nagari padas (3.2), but the nagari motif in it is only the address "friend": in substance it praises Gaura in the image of the wish-fulfilling tree. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). called. "Wish-fulfilling tree" (kalpataru) — an image known from CC (Adi 9: the Lord is both the gardener and the tree of prema itself, giving its fruits to all). GPT1 notes a variant of the first line: "What shall I say, friend, of a wondrous thing!" yearning, not the arati rite. Instead of this couplet GPT1 gives a variant: "the bee-devotees seek the wish-fulfilling tree [of His feet]; says Vasu: wondrous is this on earth"; instead of 1.4b — "many bhavas arose, but the hope was not fulfilled." KGC: "its shade nourishes" (poṣe), GPT: "enter its shade" (paise).

2. Vasu Ghosha — "āju mui ki dekhilum̐ gorā naṭarāya…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 23; GCd, no. 12)

Nagari-bhava. "What have I seen today — Gora, the king of dancers!" The Creator made Him, putting in so much rasa; His body surpasses gold, His face a hundred moons, His eyes steal the hearts of women; on the bank of the Suradhuni Gorachand shines. Raga dhanashi.5

আজু মুই কি দেখিলুঁ গোরা নটরায় ।
অসীম মহিমা গোরার কহনে না যায় ॥

āju mui ki dekhilum̐ gorā naṭarāya |
asīma mahimā gorāra kahane nā yāya ||

āju — today; mui ki dekhilum̐ — what have I seen; gorā naṭarāya — Gora, the king of dancers; asīma mahimā gorāra — Gora's boundless glory; kahane nā yāya — cannot be told

2.1What have I seen today — Gora, the king of dancers!
Gora's boundless glory cannot be told.

কেমনে গঢ়ল বিধি কত রস দিয়া ।
ঢল ঢল গোরা-তনু কাঞ্চন জিনিয়া ॥

kemane gaṛhala bidhi kata rasa diyā |
ḍhala ḍhala gorā-tanu kāñcana jiniyā ||

kemane gaṛhala bidhi — how did the Creator fashion; kata rasa diyā — putting in so much rasa; ḍhala ḍhala — rippling, overflowing; gorā-tanu — Gora's body; kāñcana jiniyā — surpassing gold

2.2How did the Creator fashion Him, putting in so much rasa!
Gora's body ripples with radiance, surpassing gold.

কত শত চাঁদ জিনি বদন-কমল ।
রমণীর চিত হরে নয়ন-যুগল ॥

kata śata cām̐da jini badana-kamala |
ramaṇīra cita hare nayana-yugala ||

kata śata cām̐da jini — surpassing hundreds of moons; badana-kamala — the lotus face; ramaṇīra cita hare — steals the hearts of women; nayana-yugala — the pair of eyes

2.3His lotus face is lovelier than hundreds of moons;
the pair of His eyes steals the hearts of women.6

বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে হইয়া বিভোর ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে গোরাচাঁদ উজোর ॥

bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe haiyā bibhora |
suradhunī-tīre gorācām̐da ujora ||

bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; haiyā bibhora — lost [in rapture]; suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni; gorācām̐da ujora — Gorachand shines

2.4Says Vasudeva Ghosha, lost in rapture:
on the bank of the Suradhuni Gorachand shines.

after VG-025). The catalogue had no row for it (new row: VG-184). Witness: the Gita-chandrodaya of Narahari Chakravarti (GCd; ed. 1948, p. 72, gaura-chandrikas to Radha's purvaraga, no. 12, raga suhai) — with the same signature; there it stands among Vasu's nagari padas known from PK (PK 2169, 28, 2172, 899, 777 — chapter 27, nos. 9, 15, 11, 17, 16). The pada is not in PK or KGC; attribution to Vasu by GPT and GCd (B). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). "how many moons," "ripples" (ḍharaḍhara), in 2.4 — "Gora has lit up the bank of the Suradhuni."

3. Vasu Ghosha — "āju mui ki pekhalum̐ gaurāṅga sundara…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 24)

Nagari-bhava. "What have I seen today — the beautiful Gauranga: in the three worlds there is no such nagara!" Noble wives are enchanted by His form, trees thrill hearing of His virtues, stones melt, beasts and birds weep, the townswomen cannot hold their hearts steady, gods, siddhas and sages are in turmoil: Gora is Madana-mohana. Raga dhanashi.7

আজু মুই কি পেখলুঁ গৌরাঙ্গ সুন্দর ।
এ তিন ভুবনে নাই এমন নাগর ॥

āju mui ki pekhalum̐ gaurāṅga sundara |
e tina bhubane nāi emana nāgara ||

āju mui ki pekhalum̐ — what have I seen today; gaurāṅga sundara — the beautiful Gauranga; e tina bhubane — in these three worlds; nāi emana nāgara — there is no such nagara

3.1What have I seen today — the beautiful Gauranga!
In these three worlds there is no such nagara.8

কুলবতী সব রূপ দেখিয়া মোহিত ।
গুণ শুনি তরু-লতা হয় পুলকিত ॥

kulabatī saba rūpa dekhiyā mohita |
guṇa śuni taru-latā haya pulakita ||

kulabatī saba — all the noble wives; rūpa dekhiyā mohita — are enchanted, seeing [His] form; guṇa śuni — hearing of [His] virtues; taru-latā — trees and creepers; haya pulakita — thrill

3.2All the noble wives are enchanted, seeing His form;
trees and creepers thrill, hearing of His virtues.

শিলা গলি গলি বহে মৃগ পাখী কাঁদে ।
নগরের নাগরী সব বুক নাহি বাঁধে ॥

śilā gali gali bahe mṛga pākhī kām̐de |
nagarera nāgarī saba buka nāhi bām̐dhe ||

śilā gali gali bahe — stones melt and flow; mṛga pākhī kām̐de — beasts and birds weep; nagarera nāgarī saba — all the women of the town; buka nāhi bām̐dhe — cannot hold their hearts steady

3.3Stones melt and flow, beasts and birds weep;
all the women of the town cannot hold their hearts steady.

সুর-সিদ্ধ-মুনিগণের মন উচাটন ।
বাসুদেব কহে গোরা মদনমোহন ॥

sura-siddha-munigaṇera mana ucāṭana |
bāsudeba kahe gorā madanamohana ||

sura-siddha-munigaṇera — of the gods, siddhas and sages; mana ucāṭana — the mind is in turmoil; bāsudeba kahe — says Vasudeva; gorā madanamohana — Gora is Madana-mohana

3.4The gods, siddhas and sages are in turmoil of heart.
Says Vasudeva: Gora is Madana-mohana.9

The pada is not in PK, KGC or GCd; attribution to Vasu by GPT only (C). It is close to Vasu's PK 2151 (chapter 27, no. 1: "birds, beasts and trees weep hearing of His virtues; noble wives cannot hold their hearts steady"), but it is a different text. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). "Cannot hold their hearts steady" (lit. "bind the breast") is a general formula of beauty (chapter 27, note 2). GPT1: "nagarī" — a misprint for "nāgarī" (GPT2).

4. Vasu Ghosha — "sajani lo gorārūpa janu kām̐cā sonā…" (GPT1 pp. 162–163, no. 19)

Nagari-bhava. "Friend, Gora's form is like pure gold: seeing it, a woman cannot stay at home." His form has fixed itself in her eyes, wherever she looks there is Gora; He seems familiar, yet she cannot make out who He is. The poet answers: "Townswoman, that is the stealer of the gopis' hearts!" Raga suhai.10

সজনি লো গোরারূপ জনু কাঁচা সোনা ।
দেখিতে নারীর মন ঘরেতে টিকে না ॥

sajani lo gorārūpa janu kām̐cā sonā |
dekhite nārīra mana gharete ṭike nā ||

sajani lo — friend; gorārūpa — Gora's form; janu kām̐cā sonā — like pure (unworked) gold; dekhite — seeing [it]; nārīra mana — a woman's heart; gharete ṭike nā — does not stay at home

4.1Friend, Gora's form is like pure gold:
seeing it, a woman cannot stay at home.

বাঁকা ভুরু বাঁকা নয়ন চাহনিতে যায় চেনা ।
ও রূপে মন দিলে সই কুলমান থাকে না ॥

bām̐kā bhuru bām̐kā nayana cāhanite yāya cenā |
o rūpe mana dile sai kulamāna thāke nā ||

bām̐kā bhuru — curved brows; bām̐kā nayana — slanting eyes; cāhanite yāya cenā — by the glance one knows [Him]; o rūpe mana dile — if one gives one's heart to that form; sai — friend; kulamāna thāke nā — the family's honour does not remain

4.2Curved brows, slanting eyes — by His glance you know Him;
give your heart to that form, friend, and no family honour remains.11

নয়নে লেগেছে রূপ না যায় পাশরা ।
যেদিকে চাই দেখিতে পাই শুধুই সেই গোরা ॥

nayane legeche rūpa nā yāya pāśarā |
yedike cāi dekhite pāi śudhui sei gorā ||

nayane legeche rūpa — the form has fixed itself in my eyes; nā yāya pāśarā — it cannot be forgotten; yedike cāi — wherever I look; dekhite pāi — I see; śudhui sei gorā — only that Gora

4.3The form has fixed itself in my eyes — I cannot forget it:
wherever I look, I see only that Gora.

চিন চিন লাগে কিন্তু চিনতে না যায় পারা ।
বাসু কহে নাগরি ঐ গোপীর মনচোরা ॥

cina cina lāge kintu cinate nā yāya pārā |
bāsu kahe nāgari ai gopīra manacorā ||

cina cina lāge — He seems familiar, so familiar; kintu cinate nā yāya pārā — but I cannot make out who He is; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; nāgari — O townswoman; ai gopīra manacorā — that is the stealer of the gopis' hearts

4.4He seems familiar, so familiar, yet I cannot make out who He is.
Says Vasu: townswoman, that is the stealer of the gopis' hearts!12

The language is late and colloquial ("legeche," "cinate," "śudhui"), which, like the absence of early witnesses, tells against Vasu's authorship (cf. Majumdar's argument on the unreliability of GPT — introductory note to the section). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). padas on Radha and Krishna; translated as in the original (introductory note, rule 2). that is why He seems familiar to her. This is a tenet of gaura-tattva (Gaura is Krishna who has taken Radha's bhava and luster; CC Adi 1.5); it does not make Gaura the hero of a love play in Navadvipa (introductory note). GPT2: "e" ("this") instead of "ai".

5. Vasu Ghosha — "nirabadhi gorārūpa dekhi…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 25)

Nagari-bhava. "Ceaselessly I see Gora's form — streams flow from my eyes": night and day the townswoman knows nothing, the jewel of brahmanas has entered her inmost heart; not seeing Gorachand's face, she cannot hold on to life. Raga dhanashi.13

নিরবধি গোরারূপ দেখি ।
নিঝরে ঝরয়ে দুটী আঁখি ॥

nirabadhi gorārūpa dekhi |
nijhare jharaye duṭī ām̐khi ||

nirabadhi — ceaselessly; gorārūpa dekhi — I see Gora's form; nijhare jharaye — stream like a waterfall; duṭī ām̐khi — both eyes

5.1Ceaselessly I see Gora's form —
from both my eyes it streams like a waterfall.

কি কহব কি হবে উপায় ।
প্রাণ মোর ধরণে না যায় ॥

ki kahaba ki habe upāya |
prāṇa mora dharaṇe nā yāya ||

ki kahaba — what shall I say; ki habe upāya — what will be the remedy; prāṇa mora — my life; dharaṇe nā yāya — cannot be held

5.2What shall I say? Where is my remedy?
My life will not stay in me.

নিশি দিশি কিছুই না জানি ।
মরমে লাগিল দ্বিজমণি ॥

niśi diśi kichui nā jāni |
marame lāgila dvijamaṇi ||

niśi diśi — night and day; kichui nā jāni — I know nothing; marame lāgila — has pierced my inmost heart; dvijamaṇi — the jewel of the twice-born

5.3Night and day I know nothing:
the jewel of brahmanas has entered my inmost heart.14

না দেখিয়া গোরাচাঁদ-মুখ ।
কহে বাসু বিদরয়ে বুক ॥

nā dekhiyā gorācām̐da-mukha |
kahe bāsu bidaraye buka ||

nā dekhiyā — not seeing; gorācām̐da-mukha — Gorachand's face; kahe bāsu — says Vasu; bidaraye buka — the breast breaks

5.4Not seeing Gorachand's face —
says Vasu — the breast breaks.

6. Vasu Ghosha — "dekhiyā āyalum̐ gorācām̐de…" (GPT1 p. 164, no. 26)

Nagari-bhava. "I have seen Gorachand — and since then my soul weeps": not seeing His moon-face, the townswoman finds no rest, household work falls from her hands; Gauranga's glory has no limit. Raga dhanashi.15

দেখিয়া আয়লুঁ গোরাচাঁদে ।
সেই হৈতে প্রাণ মোর কাঁদে ॥

dekhiyā āyalum̐ gorācām̐de |
sei haite prāṇa mora kām̐de ||

dekhiyā āyalum̐ — I came back having seen; gorācām̐de — Gorachand; sei haite — since then; prāṇa mora kām̐de — my soul weeps

6.1I came back having seen Gorachand —
and since then my soul weeps.

মন মোর করে ছন ছন ।
না দেখিলে ও চাঁদ-বদন ॥

mana mora kare chana chana |
nā dekhile o cām̐da-badana ||

mana mora — my heart; kare chana chana — is restless, finds no rest; nā dekhile — when I do not see; o cām̐da-badana — that moon-face

6.2My heart is restless, finds no peace,
when I do not see that moon-face.

গৃহকাজে নাহি রহে চিত ।
না দেখিয়া গৌর-চরিত ॥

gṛhakāje nāhi rahe cita |
nā dekhiyā gaura-carita ||

gṛhakāje — on household work; nāhi rahe cita — the mind does not stay; nā dekhiyā — not seeing; gaura-carita — Gaura's deeds

6.3My mind will not stay on household work
when I do not see Gaura's deeds.

অনুপম গৌরাঙ্গ-মহিমা ।
বাসুদেব না পায়েন সীমা ॥

anupama gaurāṅga-mahimā |
bāsudeba nā pāyena sīmā ||

anupama — matchless; gaurāṅga-mahimā — Gauranga's glory; bāsudeba — Vasudeva; nā pāyena sīmā — finds no limit

6.4Matchless is Gauranga's glory:
Vasudeva finds no limit to it.16

7. Vasu Ghosha — "so bahuballabha gorā jagatera manacorā…" (GPT1 pp. 163–164, no. 22)

Nagari-bhava. "Gora is beloved of many, He steals the hearts of all the world — why then should I want Him to be mine alone? Yet whose heart can bear the sharing!" The townswoman gives family, honour, life and youth for the treasure that is Gora; without Him she will enter the waters of the Suradhuni. Raga vibhasa.17

সো বহুবল্লভ গোরা জগতের মনচোরা
তবে কেন আমার করিতে চাই একা ।
হেন ধন অন্যে দিতে পারে বল কার চিতে
ভাগাভাগি নাহি যায় দেখা ॥

so bahuballabha gorā jagatera manacorā
tabe kena āmāra karite cāi ekā |
hena dhana anye dite pāre bala kāra cite
bhāgābhāgi nāhi yāya dekhā ||

so bahuballabha gorā — He, Gora, beloved of many; jagatera manacorā — the stealer of the world's hearts; tabe kena — why then; āmāra karite cāi ekā — do I want to make Him mine alone; hena dhana — such a treasure; anye dite — to give to another; pāre bala kāra cite — say, whose heart can bear; bhāgābhāgi — sharing; nāhi yāya dekhā — cannot be borne to see

7.1He is Gora, beloved of many, the stealer of all the world's hearts —
why then do I want Him to be mine alone?

Summary of Chapter 28

Chapter 28 completes the nagari padas of Vasu Ghosha: after the 25 padas from PK (chapter 27), here are 15 padas known from GPT (two of them also have other witnesses: KGC — no. 1, the *Gita-chandrodaya — no. 2; three are new to the catalogue: nos. 2, 5, 6). Majumdar considers GPT unreliable for Vasu; one of these padas (no. 13) he explicitly calls a reworking of a pada on Krishna. Then come the nagari padas of other poets from the same pallavas of PK ("Gauranga's form — the words of the nagaris," gaura-chandrikas to purvaraga, anuraga, the dream, the reproaches to the elders): Nayanananda (5), Yadu (2), Murari (2), Balarama Dasa, Chandrashekhara, Lochana Dasa (2). The padas of Yadunandana from the Bhakti-ratnakara (12th wave, pp. 904–910: the words of the "anuragavatis" — women of Nadia in love with Gaura — in Narahari Chakravarti's narrative) are assigned to chapter 29, together with Narahari Chakravarti's padas from the same cycle and from section 3.2 of GPT. The pada GPT1 4.4 no. 12 "…ḍākātera pirīti…" (signed Vasu) is PK 2531, Radha's words without Gaura (excluded already in chapter 9); Lochana's pada PK 2219 is about the sannyasa, not nagari-bhava; the pada KR-003 (PK 2018) is not nagari (translated in chapter 11).*
